lead: `tools/splice.py` and `tools/session.py` take a patch in two different formats, and the wrap skeleton is the one you will have read most recently.
body: A splice patch is git conflict markers — `--- <path>`, then `<<<<<<< OLD` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> NEW` around each block — while a wrap file's `## plan-edit:` is `--- old` / `--- new`, and writing the wrap form into a splice patch is refused with a message that names the fix but not the shape. `python tools/splice.py --help` prints the invocation forms and the patch format.
